comparison: Perfect agreement on productivity inversion claims (C12-C14, C63-C65, C197-C209, C222-C224). Both recognize this as a key finding that explains experimental observations from Ding et al. 2023. Peer reviewer explicitly praises this as a strength that provides rigorous explanation for previously unexplained experimental phenomena.

Perfect agreement on model limitations (C225-C238). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the coarse-grained approach as appropriate. Peer reviewers acknowledge the model is 'carefully and realistically created' and qualitatively reproduces experimental features, validating the authors' justifications for simplifications.

Strong agreement on dimer effects (C165-C178, C219). Both find these claims supported. Peer reviewers do not challenge the findings about dimers' negative impact, accepting them as part of the validated systematic exploration of pool compositions.

Disagreement on prior work context (C44-C46). OpenEval finds these claims properly cite Chamanian and Higgs work, but Peer Reviewer 2 questions whether the current error mechanism has 'the same nature as sequence scrambling' from prior work, indicating need for clarification of the relationship.

Strong agreement on ligation types and fidelity issues (C6, C50-C56, C213-C215). Both recognize the three ligation types and their roles. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly affirms that 'ligation of oligomers from VCG itself results in a high error rate,' directly supporting these findings.

Strong agreement on kinetic suppression (C9, C61-C62, C179-C181, C220). Both recognize this as a key solution. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly highlights this as a strength, noting it 'supports the claim that the separation of activation and replication chemistry is required for efficient non-enzymatic replication.'

Agreement on long oligomer dominance (C154-C155, C218). Both find these claims supported. Peer reviewers accept these findings as consistent with the validated modeling framework, with no challenges raised.

Strong agreement on fidelity-yield trade-off and oligomer length effects (C7-C8, C57-C60, C127, C129, C217). Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly affirms 'the length (longer is better) and concentration (intermediate is better) of the VCG oligos have an outsized impact on the fidelity and yield.' Both recognize these as important findings.

Strong agreement on modeling methodology (C47-C49, C104, C122-C124). All peer reviewers explicitly praise the kinetic model as 'carefully and realistically created' (Reviewer 3), 'high-quality theoretical modeling' (Reviewer 2), with 'convincing theoretical arguments' (Editor). No concerns raised about methodology.

Agreement on oligomer length scaling (C242, C244). Both find these conclusions supported. Peer reviewers accept this follows from the validated modeling framework, with Editor noting 'convincing theoretical arguments' about VCG features.

Partial disagreement on characteristic lengths (C132). OpenEval finds this supported by modeling results, but Peer Reviewer 2 states the authors 'introduce two important lengths LS1 and LS2 only in the conclusions and do not explain enough which each of them is important,' requesting earlier and clearer discussion.

Disagreement on regime choice and adiabatic approximation (C111-C113). OpenEval finds the approach well-justified, but Peer Reviewer 2 questions whether 'the study is done is a somewhat suboptimal regime' where 'most hybridization events do not lead to a ligation,' challenging the validity of the adiabatic approximation.
